sources.label: Network
sources.evidence: Live HTTP 200 HTML lists Seoul in Asia and shows dc__location--krse with an ordinary active pin, unlike the separate planned-pin class used for planned cities. The web reader timed out, so the live page was fetched directly.

sources.label: Network status
sources.evidence: The live status page lists Seoul, code krse, as operational under Asia.

sources.label: Pricing
sources.evidence: The pricing page grants access to the entire network. Asia/Oceania bandwidth is $0.08/GB for the first 10 TB/month, $0.06 for the next 40 TB, $0.04 for the next 50 TB, and $0.02 above 100 TB. It lists a $4 monthly minimum, $49 minimum payment, and no request charges.

limitations: Published location and plan access do not prove that a particular Korean ISP will be routed to Seoul.

sources.label: Network FAQ
sources.evidence: The live FAQ states 28 global PoPs and 9 SuperPoPs and links its map to https://www.belugacdn.com/map.pdf.

sources.label: Network map (2016)
sources.evidence: Downloaded the live PDF and visually inspected its single rendered page. It is explicitly titled BelugaCDN Network Map 2016, shows Seoul with the ordinary PoP marker, and carries a 2016 copyright. It does not establish current operations or plan eligibility.

sources.label: CDN pricing
sources.evidence: The live product page advertises $0.01/GB global bandwidth. Its pay-as-you-go details state $10 prepayment for 1,000 GB and a $1 active-account monthly fee. No Seoul-specific availability or billing conditions are given.

limitations: The linked map is ten years old, even though the current FAQ still links to it.
Do not interpret unconfirmed as proof that Seoul is absent.
Global headline pricing is not confirmation of current Seoul access.

sources.label: CDN technology
sources.evidence: Live HTTP 200 page fetched directly after web-reader failure. It states that scrubbing nodes also cache content, describes regions including Asia, and says every protected website uses the CDN by default. It gives no Seoul city-level confirmation.

sources.label: Website Protection plans
sources.evidence: Live HTTP 200 page lists Basic at $100/month for one domain. The FAQ describes built-in CDN on every plan and no separate charges for legitimate or attack bandwidth. Caching is enabled by default. These general website-protection terms do not identify a Seoul location.

sources.label: Global and Asia connections
sources.evidence: The live page distinguishes Global from Asia connectivity and discusses direct Asian infrastructure connections through Twin Tunnel or PNI. It neither names Seoul nor establishes the equivalent website-protection plan access.

limitations: Regional coverage does not confirm a Seoul cache.
The Asia connection option should not be silently equated with a Seoul website CDN plan.

records.planNote: Confirm Seoul availability for FLEX; dedicated infrastructure is separately quoted.

sources.label: Network and company
sources.evidence: The live page describes 25+ locations across Europe, Asia and America, but provides no city inventory. It lists KINX and SK Broadband among APAC carriers; carrier names alone do not establish a Seoul cache. Enterprise customization is described separately.

sources.label: FLEX pricing
sources.evidence: The live pricing page describes FLEX Anycast CDN at $5/TB initially with a $25 monthly minimum, then marginal volume tiers down to $2.50/TB. It advertises a common price for US, Europe and Asia, without naming Seoul. Dedicated CDN infrastructure is quoted separately from the shared network.

limitations: A search-indexed older version of the vendor blog's how-youtube-cdn-works article mentioned Seoul, but reopening that URL live returned a revised article without Seoul. The stale snippet was not accepted as current PoP proof.
Public global pricing and Korean carrier names are not confirmation of Seoul plan access.
No independent latency or edge-location measurements were performed.

sources.label: CDN network and pricing
sources.evidence: The live page states all CDN nodes are available on the plan at one global rate and lists $4/$3/$2 per TB tiers plus $20 setup including 5 TB. Its embedded public location data includes Seoul (id 117, latitude 37.56, longitude 126.99), with is_cdn_deployed:false, is_colocation_deployed:true, and is_ip_transit_deployed:true. A generic Seoul company location must not be presented as a deployed CDN PoP.

sources.label: CDN billing FAQ
sources.evidence: The live CDN microsite repeats the $4/$3/$2 per TB rates and $20 setup including 5 TB. It describes 30 global locations, compared with 23 on the main product page, but does not identify Seoul.

limitations: The public embedded location data is a vendor inventory, not a measurement of actual traffic routing.
The two official pages disagree on total CDN location count; neither is evidence of Seoul access.
Use unconfirmed rather than a categorical claim that FDC has no Seoul CDN.
